The centered side-1/2 square stays inside T, and its positively oriented half gives area 1/8>L². Thus the quota L² is unavoidable at c and equality means saturation on E_L and no T,D mass.

For the own square uniqueness, choose a minimizing ellipsoid-normalized u at the center. Its opposite is minimizing by symmetry. If the displacement has nonzero u-projection, one cap strictly loses own mass. Otherwise the same cap has unchanged mass and would be minimizing at both marks. Differentiating the integral along a tangent gives the written strip integral, with null kink lines and bounded directional quotient. The common positive strip forces the displacement orthogonal to all tangents, hence parallel to Σu. Its zero u-projection then forces zero.

At zero width (2−4σ)^2/2=2−8σ+8σ². Adding the triangle's bound [2,2+(9/2)σ²] gives the exact interval in the statement, strictly between the squares of the L endpoints. Dominated convergence off null affine lines, compactness of the normal circle, and the implicit triangle continuation give the endpoint sign persistence and IVT tie.

Pure-base cuts isolate the two endpoint fibers, each with small total mass. The square and triangle have the same maximum near two and no other marks at that level. The midpoint assignments (−1+1)/2=0 and (2+0)/2=1 are same-parity and use the actual two deepest bases.
